newsitem.title: CANADA: Multiple CWB grain export cases to be tried as one.
newsitem.headline: Multiple CWB grain export cases to be tried as one.

text.p: The first 30 farmers to face a court on charges stemming from a series of wheat and barley shipments into the United States in 1996 without Canadian Wheat Board export permits agreed to have one case tried, a prosecutor said.
"They've all agreed on one test case. It's the same charge and pretty well all the same facts," Crown prosecutor Clyde Bond said.
Several farmers trucked CWB grains to the U.S. and face fines of more than C$500,000. One farmer tried on the same charges in the spring, was acquitted on a technicality.
Two other farmers also tried in the spring on the same charges were convicted, fined and one remains in prison.
Those three farmers crossed the U.S. border without CWB permits in 1993 and 1994.
The 30 farmers who appeared in an Estevan, Sask., court on Monday were the first to face a court on charges brought this year, Canada Customs spokesman Ron Ferniuk said.
"There's a number of trials scheduled for November, December and then through January, February, March and April. This group's pretrial hearing has been put over to January 8," Ferniuk said.
The clause under which one farmer was acquitted was amended by Canada's federal cabinet one hour after the ruling.

Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale admitted at the time that the Canadian Wheat Board's export monopoly in wheat and barley was in doubt based on the ruling and the regulation had been clarified by the cabinet order.
